subject: Literature
title: Nella Larsen and the Harlem Renaissance
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nella Larsen and the Harlem Renaissance usable.

hook.text: Nella Larsen wrote two brilliant novels about race and identity, then vanished from literature to work as a nurse.

buildup.text: Quicksand and Passing explored the psychological cost of living between racial identities in 1920s America.

discovery.text: Passing follows two light-skinned Black women, one who 'passes' as white, forging a bond charged with envy and danger.

twist.text: Larsen was falsely accused of plagiarism, and the humiliation drove her out of the literary world permanently.

climax.text: Larsen's rediscovery showed how racism and sexism conspired to silence one of America's most perceptive voices.

punchline.text: The literary world lost her, but her novels outlived the silence.

quiz.question: Why did Larsen stop writing literature?
options: She lost interest in fiction and pursued science
A false accusation of plagiarism drove her from the literary world
Her publisher refused to print works by Black women
